Subject: MedSys — purchase path & contract lane: post-demo next steps

Hi Ava / Carlos — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth.

Recap (short):
- Demo covered integration points with your data lake + clinical inference flow.
- Primary use case: reduce annotation backlog for clinical review (pilot scope = 3 clinics, ~2500 docs/week).
- Key success metric: 20% reduction in manual review time in pilot.

Buying/process questions we need confirmed to map the lane:
1) Economic buyer: is Carlos still the approver for pilots > $25k? Please confirm who signs off on pilot POs.
2) Procurement owner & cadence: who will own the contract queue (name + email)?
3) Security/Legal gating: do you require an NDA first, or can we proceed with a standard MSA + DPA draft?
4) Target start: you mentioned late Jan — can we get an internal procurement sync by Dec 8 to align on turn times?

Proposed Redwood owners (who will run coordination):
- Contract routing & redlines: Monica (commercial/legal coordination)
- Security/compliance evidence: Rishi (technical/soc2/KMS questions)
- Day-to-day pilot ops: Logan (PM)

Suggested next steps (if that works):
- Ava: confirm economic buyer and procurement contact (reply)
- Procurement: we can intake your security questionnaire — feel free to send the doc (we'll respond within 3 business days).
- Redwood: Monica will prepare a draft NDA + MSA baseline and a redline tracker for sequencing.

I attached a one-pager SOW template and will circulate a redline tracker once Monica confirms. If useful, we can propose a sequencing: NDA -> Security questionnaire -> MSA redline -> DPA sign-off (typical turn times: NDA 1-2 business days, DPA 3-5 business days, MSA redline depends on complexity; we'll propose a 7 business day target for first pass).

Thanks — looking forward to keeping momentum.

Best,
Logan Wright

Hi Ava / Sally / Carlos — looping in next steps and a proposed contract-routing playbook so procurement has visibility into owners and expected turn times.

High-level owner map (Redwood):
- NDA: owned by Redwood commercial (Monica) for execution; proposed turnaround 1 business day for standard mutual NDA. If MedSys needs bespoke terms, allow 2-3 business days.
- MSA: primary redline owner will be Redwood Legal + Monica coordinating comments; we will post an initial baseline MSA for MedSys to redline. Proposed first-pass target: 7 business days from receipt of MedSys redlines.
- DPA: Rishi will own technical review; Redwood can provide a standard DPA template. Target turnaround: 3 business days for standard changes; complex privacy clauses (e.g., EU data residency) may take longer.

Redline sequencing (recommended):
1) Execute NDA quickly (if required) so we can exchange minimal datasets for pilot testing.
2) Intake Security Questionnaire (Ava already sent) — Rishi to triage and tag high-priority items for remediation or SOC2 evidence.
3) Exchange MSA baseline -> track comments in central redline_tracker.xlsx -> Redwood legal will queue responses in priority order (econ buyer/finance must approve material commercial changes).
4) DPA sign-off in parallel once MSA commercial terms are stable.

Suggested turn times (to set expectations with Procurement):
- NDA: 1-3 business days
- Security questionnaire triage: 3 business days to initial response, 7 business days for detailed evidence gathering
- MSA initial redline cycle: 7 business days
- Subsequent redline cycles: 3-5 business days each (dependent on scope)

Monica will own the redline_tracker and will push updates into the shared Drive folder (link below). Rishi — once you've triaged, can you highlight any items that would change the pilot acceptance criteria?

If MedSys confirms Dec 8 at 10am PT for the procurement sync, Monica and Rishi will join and we will bring a pre-populated redline tracker and an NDA template for signature.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Head of Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Thanks — quick technical note from the compliance side so MedSys knows what to expect during triage: 

- SOC 2 evidence: we can provide our SOC 2 Type II report and select control narratives in the first 3 business days after NDA execution.
- Data handling / DPA: the DPA will need to cover access controls, KMS usage, and retention. If MedSys requires customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS), that will add ~7 business days to the setup timeline.
- PHI-adjacent examples: if you need sample PHI-flagged documents for pilot tuning, we'd prefer a redacted sample set behind an NDA.

On the security questionnaire: I've started the triage and flagged 6 items as high-priority (data residency, audit logs, encryption-at-rest, key management, SSO provisioning, and incident notification SLA). I will send a triage summary prior to the Dec 8 sync.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Security PM | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
